topic: What If the Moon Came Twice as Close? (Vertical Short)
title: WHAT IF THE MOON
CAME 2X CLOSER?

script.beat: 0 cold open hook (0-4s): beach, giant Moon, MOON 2X CLOSER
script.text: The Moon just moved twice as close. Watch what the ocean does first.

script.beat: 1 payoff: tide climbing PULL x8 (192,200 km vs 384,400 km)
script.text: Waves race up the beach, because halving the Moon's three hundred eighty-four thousand, four hundred kilometre distance to about one hundred ninety-two thousand, two hundred kilometres makes its pull grow about eight times stronger.

script.beat: 2 sky size x2 wide, x4 area
script.text: Overhead, the Moon looks about twice as wide and covers about four times the area in the sky.

script.beat: 3 supermoon reality check: only 14% bigger and 30% brighter (NASA)
script.text: According to NASA, a real supermoon is only up to fourteen percent bigger and thirty percent brighter than the faintest full Moon, while this giant is one hundred percent wider.
Nights turn bright enough to read a book outdoors while you move your beach towel up the stairs again and again.

script.beat: 5 reality: Moon drifts 1 inch a year
script.text: In reality, the Moon drifts about one inch farther away every year.

script.beat: 6 end CTA: Supermoon 24 Nov + loop to frame 0
script.text: Supermoon twenty-fourth of November. Full film on the channel.

science.claim: The Moon's average distance from Earth is 384,400 km (238,855 mi), its radius is 1,740 km, it orbits Earth in 27 days, and it drifts away by about 1 inch per year.
science.working: Direct NASA lunar fact sheet values: mean orbit distance 384,400 km (238,855 miles), equatorial/mean radius 1,740 km, sidereal orbital period 27 days, lunar laser ranging recession ~1 inch/year.

science.claim: The Moon's orbit is slightly oval, with perigee at ~363,300 km (226,000 mi) and apogee at ~405,500 km (251,000 mi); a supermoon looks up to 14% bigger and 30% brighter than the faintest full Moon, can cause higher tides than usual, and occurs on 24 Nov 2026 at 14:54 UTC and 24 Dec 2026.
science.working: At perigee (~363,300 km) vs apogee (~405,500 km), apparent angular diameter increases by up to ~14% and illuminated flux by ~30%; alignment of full Moon with perigee produces perigean spring tides.

science.claim: In November 2026, Mars and Jupiter appear 1.2 degrees apart before sunrise on 15-16 Nov; the Leonid meteor shower peaks on 17-18 Nov after moonset with up to ~15 meteors per hour; the 24 Nov supermoon is the first of three supermoons in a row across November, December, and January.
science.working: Skywatching calendar dates and rates directly from NASA's November 2026 guide.

science.claim: At half of the average distance (about 192,200 km), the Moon appears about twice as wide (100% wider), covers about four times the area in the sky, and exerts about eight times the tidal pull.
science.working: Half of 384,400 km = 192,200 km. Apparent angular width scales as 1/d = 2x (100% wider); solid-angle sky area scales as (1/d)^2 = 4x; differential gravitational tidal force scales as inverse cube (1/d)^3 = 2^3 = 8x.
science.source: Computed from NASA Moon Facts https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/ and inverse-cube tidal physics
